CANONICAL_NAME.value: Indirect self-tuning regulator (Astrom & Wittenmark, Adaptive Control ch. 3): RLS with forgetting factor estimates the plant online, pole-placement (R,S,T) recomputed every step -- a MATLAB implementation, run under Octave

value.lineage: The self-tuning regulator (Astrom & Wittenmark 1973; textbook Adaptive Control 1989/1995, Example 3.5-style: model-following with zero cancellation): a recursive-least-squares estimator with forgetting tracks the plant's a1,a2,b0,b1; the controller polynomials R,S,T are re-derived from the estimates each sample so the closed loop follows the reference model Am/Bm. This is a student's faithful implementation of the textbook algorithm (MATLAB, 2020) with the true plant's parameters drawn as reference lines -- the ORACLE the estimates converge to (a1=-1.6065, a2=0.6065, b0=0.1065, b1=0.0902).

cut.note: the indirect adaptive controller in its textbook form: at every sample a recursive least-squares estimator with exponential forgetting updates the plant's four parameters from the last two inputs and outputs; the controller polynomials R, S, T are then re-derived from the estimates by pole placement against a fixed reference model; the control is applied and the loop repeats. The script runs the design twice: cancelling the plant zero (a division by b0, which fails for a non-minimum-phase plant) and not cancelling it (the Diophantine solution with the extra observer pole a0)

organs.human_name: rls_forgetting.m: k = P phi' / (lambda + phi P phi'); P = (P - k phi P) / lambda; theta = theta + k (y - phi theta); main_code.m: phi = [-y(t), -y(t-1), u(t), u(t-1)], lambda = 0.8, P0 = diag(100, 100, 1, 1), theta0 = [0, 0, 0.01, 0.2]
organs.mechanism: the plant is modelled as y(t+1) = -a1 y(t) - a2 y(t-1) + b0 u(t) + b1 u(t-1); each sample forms the regressor from the last two outputs and inputs, computes the gain from the covariance, corrects the parameter estimate by the prediction error, and shrinks the covariance with a forgetting factor of 0.8 so old data is discounted geometrically; the initial covariance is large on the a's and small on the b's, and b0 starts at 0.01 rather than 0 so the first division in the design is finite
assumptions: the plant is linear, second order and slowly varying (forgetting makes the estimator track drift at the price of noise sensitivity); the regressor is persistently excited (the square-wave reference supplies it)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: O(n^2) per step, no matrix inversion; the estimator the textbook builds every adaptive scheme on
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: with lambda = 0.8 and no excitation the covariance grows without bound (estimator wind-up), which the script avoids only because the reference keeps switching; b0 near zero makes the design explode
organs.human_prior: Astrom & Wittenmark 1989/1995 Adaptive Control, chapter 2 (RLS with forgetting)

organs.human_name: main_code.m experiment 1 (28-33): r1 = b1/b0, s0 = (am1 - a1)/b0, s1 = (am2 - a2)/b0, t0 = bm0/b0 (zero cancelled); experiment 2 (125-140): r1, s0, s1 from the Diophantine identity with the observer pole a0 and t0 = (1 + am1 + am2)/(b0 + b1), a0 re-estimated as (a2 r1 + b1 s1)/am2; the control law u(t+1) = -r1 u(t) + t0 uc(t) [+ t1 uc(t-1)] - s0 y(t) - s1 y(t-1); reference model am1 = -1.3205, am2 = 0.4966, bm0 = 0.1761
organs.mechanism: with the estimated plant (A, B) and a desired closed-loop denominator Am (from the reference model), solve for R, S such that A R + B S = Am (times an observer polynomial) and set T so the closed loop's DC gain matches the model; variant 1 cancels the plant zero by dividing by b0 (a one-line design that requires the zero to be stable); variant 2 keeps the zero, adds an observer pole a0 and solves the 2x2 identity in closed form; the estimated a0 is updated from the previous solution; the design runs at every sample from the current estimates (certainty equivalence)
assumptions: the estimates are the truth (certainty equivalence); the reference model's poles are achievable; in variant 1 the plant zero is inside the unit circle
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the closed loop follows the reference model once the estimates converge (the plots in the script show a1, a2, b0, b1 reaching -1.6065, 0.6065, 0.1065, 0.0902, the simulated plant's true values)
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: variant 1 divides by b0, so a small or wrong b0 estimate produces huge gains (the record's 'zero cancellation' caveat); the simulated plant's zero at -0.847 is stable so variant 1 happens to work here
organs.human_prior: Astrom & Wittenmark 1995, Example 3.5 (indirect STR with and without zero cancellation)
organs.source_boundary: the design lines of both experiments

pressures.condition: an organism controls a second-order plant whose parameters it does not know; a reference model prescribes the closed-loop response to a square wave; the score is tracking error after the transient and the peak control effort; the plant may have a non-minimum-phase zero in some instances
pressures.resource_or_constraint: one RLS update and one polynomial solve per sample
pressures.failure_condition: divergence during the transient (gains from bad estimates), or instability from cancelling an unstable zero
pressures.world_punishes: fixed-gain control on a drifting plant; zero cancellation on the non-minimum-phase instance
pressures.world_rewards: forgetting-factor estimation with a bounded initial b0 and a design that keeps the zero
pressures.observable_consequence: tracking error and peak |u| over time for variant 1 vs variant 2 on the script's plant and on a plant with the zero moved outside the unit circle; estimate trajectories against the true theta
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: the true parameters as the initial estimate (the cheat control)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism initialised at the true theta with lambda = 1 must track the model from the first sample; variant 1 on the unstable-zero plant must diverge; variant 2 must not: the world must show all three
